text: The authors state that LLMs are probabilistic models whose hypothesis class is only a subset of all mappings from problems to solutions, so their empirical setup does not exactly match the theorem's assumptions, and that for nonconvex players such as neural networks there are no formal guarantees of finding a Stackelberg equilibrium efficiently; they instead train with coordinate descent toward an approximate local equilibrium.
title: Theory assumes an unrestricted deterministic prover class; LLM training does not match it
